A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Align-SLM and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Existing content can be matched reliably across appendix and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Align-SLM benchmark experiments, human meaningfulness ratings in Table 3, and appendix analyses of curriculum learning and score distributions.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and adds sampled continuations with Mistral scores in the new Table 4.

M1.justification: The TWIST-based architecture, speech processing components, preference-selection rules, LoRA DPO training, and curriculum procedure are unchanged. New Appendix C illustrates the existing selection procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain LibriSpeech and English MLS training coverage and the same lexical, syntactic, spoken StoryCloze, and speech-continuation evaluations. The added example stays within the existing continuation task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–3 is unchanged, including the pre-trained and next-token fine-tuned controls, prior SLMs and ASR+LLM in Table 2, and the re-synthesized target in Table 3.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, model sizes, evaluation metrics, training budgets, and the 100-prompt human evaluation with 10 raters per sample are retained. Appendix A specifies five sampled continuations in both versions.

E4.justification: New Appendix C/Table 4 adds a single-prompt qualitative case examining Mistral scores and the resulting chosen, rejected, and filtered candidates. Existing curriculum, data-scaling, score-distribution, and continuation analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same MMOS confidence-interval reporting. Neither repeated-run or seed reporting nor statistical estimation procedures change; the existing Pearson correlation analysis is retained.

E6.justification: New Table 4 adds five sampled continuations with Mistral scores of 3, 1, 2, 1, and 3. Existing benchmark scores, human ratings, plotted results, and earlier continuation examples are unchanged.

T1.justification: The auto-BLEU definition and Equations (1)–(3), including preference selection and the DPO objective, are unchanged. Appendix C applies existing thresholds without introducing new mathematical definitions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty, semantic-improvement, curriculum-learning, and state-of-the-art claims. The additional illustration does not expand their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds a local interpretation of the new examples: the lowest-scoring continuations are semantically unrelated to the prompt, supporting the usefulness of LLM feedback. Existing broader interpretations and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware, checkpoint selection, subjective-evaluation details, evaluator prompts, and resource links are unchanged. The worked example adds no new implementation requirement or reproducibility setting.

R1.justification: The reference lists and related-work discussion are unchanged. Positioning against speech-only and text-guided SLMs and earlier preference-optimization work remains the same.

P1.justification: v2 adds the explanatory Appendix C and a pointer from Section 3.2.2, reletters subsequent appendices, and makes limited wording edits. The main narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: A new single-column Table 4 is added. Former Tables 4 and 5 become Tables 5 and 6, and appendix content reflows, including moving the sample-count table to the right column on page 14. Existing figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 explains preference selection through rules and distributions; v2 adds a concrete worked example in Appendix C/Table 4 showing accepted, rejected, and filtered candidates. This modestly improves clarity and makes the selection decisions easier to inspect, while the core experimental evidence remains unchanged.
